# `Q-3-10` — Inline Note Definition Not Supported

> Inline note definitions (`[^id]: content`) cannot be rendered
> in this output format because content coalescing is not yet
> implemented.

## What this means

There are two ways to write a footnote in qmd:

- **Inline footnotes**, where the note text sits where the
  reference appears: `text^[note content]`.
- **Note definitions**, where the reference and the definition
  are separated: `text[^1]` plus a later `[^1]: note content`.

The current writer for this output format does not yet implement
the second form. To render the note in-place, it would need to
collect every definition and weave each one back to its
reference — a step the writer does not yet perform.

## Why this happens

Your document uses the `[^id]: content` form for a footnote, and
the output format you selected has not been taught to coalesce
those into their references.

## How to fix

Rewrite the footnote inline:

```markdown
A claim that needs a citation.^[Smith 2020, p. 42.]
```

instead of:

```markdown
A claim that needs a citation.[^smith]

[^smith]: Smith 2020, p. 42.
```

Both render the same in formats that *do* support coalescing
(such as HTML); rewriting to the inline form is the
lowest-friction workaround when the output format does not.

## Related

- `Q-3-11` — the same limitation for *fenced* note definitions,
  where the note body is a multi-paragraph fenced block.
- `Q-3-54` — note definitions are also not supported in ANSI
  output, for a different reason: ANSI has no way to place
  footnotes at all.
